pages.title: Laying Eggs
pages.text: Only female chickens lay eggs. A hen lays one about every in-game day (plus a random 1~3 hours).$(br2)Only after a $(bold)domesticated hen has mated with a rooster$() are the eggs she lays over the next day or so $(bold)fertilized$(); hens that never mated, and wild hens, lay normal eggs only.

pages.title: Fertilized Eggs
pages.text: Fertilized eggs have a special tooltip that also names the species. To hatch one, place it on a $(bold)hay block$() that $(bold)cannot see the sky$(). After 1 in-game day (20 minutes), a chick will hatch.$(br2)A chick from a fertilized egg is $(bold)domesticated from birth$() - no need to feed it again.$(br2)With Jade installed, looking at an incubating egg also shows its incubation progress.

pages.title: Nine Eggs Per Hay Block
pages.text: Hold fertilized eggs and right-click the $(bold)top face$() of a hay block to place them all at once - $(bold)up to 9$(), laid out in a neat 3x3 grid.$(br2)Each egg keeps its own timer and hatches on its own. Eggs are locked onto the grid, so neither water flow nor collisions can push them away.

pages.title: Getting Them Back
pages.text: Right-click the top face of the hay block with an $(bold)empty hand or any item$() to $(bold)take back one egg$() (the nearest one). It goes into your inventory, or drops at your feet if you are full.$(br2)You can also right-click the egg itself. Incubating eggs are never auto-picked-up.

pages.title: Important Notes
pages.text: Normal eggs never hatch when thrown. $(bold)Fertilized eggs can also be thrown$(), but they will never hatch either - only placing them on a sheltered hay block will hatch them.$(br2)A fertilized egg stops incubating and can be taken back if exposed to the sky or if the hay block is removed.$(br2)The hay block must be $(bold)out of sight of the sky$() - an open-air block will never hatch anything, so build a roof over it.
